module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Dubner's conjecture

*Reference*: [Every even number greater than 4208 is the sum of two t-primes](https://scispace.com/pdf/twin-prime-conjectures-3icaxy6b0m.pdf)
by *Harvey Dubner*.
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace DubnerConjecture

/--
A twin prime is a prime number that has a prime gap of 2, meaning either p - 2 or p + 2
is also prime.
-/
def IsTwinPrime (p : ℕ) : Prop :=
  p.Prime ∧ ((p - 2).Prime ∨ (p + 2).Prime)

@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem t1 : ¬IsTwinPrime 2 := by
  norm_num [IsTwinPrime]

@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem t2 : IsTwinPrime 3 := by
  norm_num [IsTwinPrime]

@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem t3 : IsTwinPrime 5 := by
  norm_num [IsTwinPrime]

@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem t4 : IsTwinPrime 101 := by
  norm_num [IsTwinPrime]

@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem t5 : ¬IsTwinPrime 100 := by
  norm_num [IsTwinPrime]

/--
Every even number greater than 4208 is the sum of two twin primes.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem dubner_conjecture (n : ℕ) (hn : 4208 < n) (h : Even n) :
    ∃ p q : ℕ,
      IsTwinPrime p ∧
      IsTwinPrime q ∧
      p + q = n := by
  sorry

end DubnerConjecture

review.notes: All seven declarations checked. The main theorem exactly states Dubner's Conjecture 4a: every even number greater than 4208 is the sum of two t-primes. IsTwinPrime matches the paper's definition, and natural-number subtraction is harmless because primality forces p ≥ 2. All five test theorems are correct and have no sorry dependency. Scratch checks compiled without errors or warnings, proved equivalence with having another prime at distance two, and proved the boundary instance 4210 = 191 + 4019 independently of the conjecture. Computation found no representation of 4208 and representations for all 100 even numbers from 4210 through 4408. No status discrepancy found. The cited SciSpace URL returned HTTP 403; the same paper was read using the OEIS-hosted copy. Experiments are in /workspace/review/scratch.lean.
